03What It IsOVERVIEW▶

Client Desk is the orchestrator of Swami's client system (Option B of the client-system plan): one skill that owns the shared setup and data, plus one module skill per channel or feature. Swami is the consultant; the person he helps is the client.

For every client, new or previous, it builds the same setup: its own Claude project, a Drive folder inside Swami's Projects folder, a private GitHub repo, a hub page and a tracker page. It keeps the shared data files in step and calls the modules a client uses. It never touches a channel itself: Messenger, email and meetings belong to the modules.

Version 1.0.1, saved on Fri Nov 27, 2026 (Eastern). One module is live today, client-messenger; the others are planned.

Why it mattersEvery client used to get a hand-built setup. Client Desk makes the names, folders, data files and pages the same every time, so any client can be picked up, updated or reopened months later without guessing where anything is.
04What It DoesOVERVIEW▶
  • IntakeAsks nine setup questions in one message (name, new or previous, title and details, source tag, channels, email, time zone, sharing, NDA), each with a default.
  • NamesBuilds every name from the answers in Swami's format, for example TestWidget(DemoPart)(JaneDoe,FB) and repo test-widget_demo-part_jane-doe_fb (a made-up client), and shows them all once before creating anything.
  • Repo AskGives Swami a one-click link to create the private repo, waits for his OK on the name, and keeps working in "no repo yet" mode meanwhile. Claude can't create a GitHub repo.
  • Data ContractWrites project.json (schema 2), comms/tracker.json and state/channels.json, the shared data contract every module reads and writes.
  • DriveCreates the client's top folder inside Projects and the numbered subfolders (01 From the client … 07 Launch, 99 Archive), reusing a folder that already exists, and records every id.
  • Build KitCopies the page builders from the private kit repo client-desk-kit into the client repo and records the kit version.
  • Hub and TrackerBuilds both pages with the kit and vibe-dashboard and publishes each as a new private artifact.
  • First UpdateRuns each enabled channel module; for a previous client that is a backfill of the whole history.
  • StatusReports status, each channel's last update, open tasks by owner, open questions and links, in a few lines.
  • Update AllOnly when Swami asks: runs every enabled module's "since last" update, then rebuilds the hub and tracker once. Never scheduled.
  • Close and ReopenPause, close or reopen a client with a dated, reasoned status log entry. Nothing is renamed or moved; reopening runs a catch-up from where each channel stopped.
  • AdoptMigrates a client set up before this skill in place, adding the schema 2 fields and rebuilding its pages to the same URLs.
  • SharingFollows the agreed rules: tracker, memory, repo, rates and NDA material always private; the client's two Drive folders and a client hub shared by email; everything else Swami's call each time.

08Capabilities and LimitationsSCOPE▶
  • Same Every TimeEvery client gets the same names, folders, data files and pages, built from one intake.
  • New or PreviousWorks for new clients and previous ones; a previous client gets a whole-history backfill.
  • No Repo YetKeeps working before the repo exists, holding files in the project folder and pushing them later.
  • Safe Status ChangesPause, close and reopen never rename or move anything, so every link keeps working, and reopening loses and duplicates nothing.
  • One Data ContractEvery module reads and writes the same three files, so modules can be added without changing the others.
  • One Live ModuleOnly client-messenger exists. Email, meetings, files, launch and the client-facing hub (client-share) are planned.
  • No Repo CreationClaude can't create or rename GitHub repos; Swami does that from the link or in GitHub settings.
  • Not Yet Run End to EndSetup hasn't been run on a client yet. The next steps are a made-up test client and then adopting the first real client.
  • Hiding Isn't PrivacyA hidden row stays in the page source, so anything the client must not see goes on a page never shared with them.
09Scheduled TasksRUNTIME▶

None. "Update all" runs only when Swami asks and is never scheduled, by his choice. No scheduled task names this skill.

11GotchasGOTCHAS▶
  • Repo Name FirstSwami asked to be advised before any repo naming action: always show the exact repo name and wait for his OK.
  • Exact SpellingsStore the client's and product's spellings at intake and use them everywhere.
  • JPEG BytesCopy each upload into /home/claude/… first, not /mnt/project-files, which rewrites JPEG bytes; hash that copy, upload it, then log the Drive link.
  • No Second FolderNever create a second Drive top folder with the same name; reuse the one that exists.
  • Old State FileA repo with state/chat-state.json keeps it until the next successful run after its contents move into state/channels.json.
  • Planned ModulesDon't improvise a planned module's job inside this skill; offer to build the module instead.
  • Windows PathsOn Windows, Drive for desktop uses a drive letter (usually G:), not ~/Library/CloudStorage; reopen PowerShell after a winget install.
12Other RequirementsREFERENCE▶
  • ConnectorsGoogle Drive connected in Claude, and the Claude GitHub app with access to the client repo and client-desk-kit.
  • Drive FolderSwami's Drive folder Projects must exist; client folders go inside it.
  • One Project per ClientEach client has its own Claude project; the skill uses the repo already attached there.
  • Code ExecutionNeeded to run the kit's builders and push the repo.
  • ComputerOptional: a Mac or a Windows 10 or 11 PC with Google Drive for desktop for local access to client files.
